items.title: Oil Prices Are Once Again on the Brink of $100
items.summary: Oil prices surge toward $100 as Houthi attacks, U.S. strikes on Iranian tankers and renewed Middle East tensions rattle markets.

items.title: Imperial Oil Stock Rises 49% YTD: Time to Hold or Lock in Profits?
items.summary: IMO's 49% year to date rally is backed by strong cash flow and Kearl growth plans, but costs, commodity swings and refinery cuts temper upside.

items.title: ExxonMobil Has Raised Its Dividend 43 Years Running. Here's the One Year the Streak Almost Broke.
items.summary: ExxonMobil is one of the most reliable dividend growers in the U.S., but that dependability was threatened in a big way in 2020.

items.title: Chevron Stock Is Near a Record High. Here’s Why the Rally May Not Be Over
items.summary: Chevron has surged more than 42% this year and is brushing against a 52-week high, but the real question is whether the fundamentals driving that run can hold at these prices or whether the easy money is already gone.

items.title: Brent crude nears $100 as Houthi strikes hit Saudi oil sites
items.summary: Houthi drones and ballistic missiles struck Saudi Aramco facilities Tuesday, wounding 73 people and deepening fears of a wider U.S.-Iran conflict

items.title: U.S. Energy Stocks Rise Premarket as Brent Approaches $100
items.summary: Shares of major U. S. energy companies moved higher in premarket trading on Tuesday as crude oil prices extended their gains amid concerns about potential disruption to Middle East energy supplies.

items.title: Premarket movers: Energy stocks rise on Iran tensions, Eaton jumps on UBS upgrade
items.summary: Investing.com -- U.S. stock futures fell early Tuesday, kicking off a shortened trading week as Wall Street monitored the U.S.-Iran conflict alongside rising trade tensions between Canada and the U.S. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.8% by 05:30 ET (09:30 GMT). S&P 500 futures fell 0.3% and Nasdaq-100 futures slipped 0.1%. U.S. markets were closed Monday for Labor Day.

items.title: Energy stocks rise premarket as oil prices climb on Middle East supply fears
items.summary: Investing.com -- Shares of major U.S. energy companies gained in premarket trading Tuesday, tracking a rise in oil prices after Iran warned that Gulf oil and gas infrastructure could be targeted in retaliation for attacks on its own assets.
